title: yunta pack manifest
description:
The pack's own identity: `publisher/name`, invoked as
`yunta run acme/review` and composed as `use: acme/qa-review`. Kept
as two plain fields rather than one combined id — `publisher` and
`name` are independently meaningful (namespacing,
`permissions.packs.publishers` matches on `publisher` alone) and
forcing every caller to split a combined string back apart would
just move the parsing problem around instead of solving it.

version.description:
Semver — no comparison logic lives here; a pack's own
version is never auto-resolved (`update` always names an exact
target ref), so nothing in v1 needs to *compare* versions,
only record and display them. Kept a plain string rather than a
`semver` dependency for the same reason [`SchemaRange`] is a
hand-rolled comparator range instead of one — add the dependency
the day something actually needs to compare two full versions,
not ahead of that need.

yunta_schema.description:
`">=1 <2"` — the same range a workflow's own `yunta_schema:`
states, read by the same parser and checked against the same
binary schema major (`yunta_core::YUNTA_SCHEMA`). `pack add`
refuses a pack whose range this binary does not satisfy.

McpServerName.description: A MCP server name: a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` or `-`

NodePermissions.description:
`permissions: read-only | edit | full` at node level — maps 1:1 onto
the adapter's session profile.

PackContents.description:
What the pack physically ships — paths relative to the pack's
own root, resolved by whoever vendors it, not by this type.

agents.description:
Agent definitions the pack ships, each a Markdown file a node or a
runner names as `publisher/agent`.

knowledge.description:
A pack can be knowledge-only (an org
knowledge-pack layer) — an empty `workflows`/`skills` with a
non-empty `knowledge` is a legitimate pack, not a degenerate one.

PackDeclares.description:
The pack's own permissions **ceiling**: `check` rejects any `prompt` or `loop`
node of the pack whose effective permissions exceed this, as an error.

executors.description:
Executable code shipped with the pack — empty means the pack is
100% declarative (YAML/prompts/skills only), auditable by
reading. A non-empty list requires explicit confirmation on
`add` and gets flagged separately by `pack audit`.

network.description:
Whether the pack's nodes may reach the network. `false`, the
default, is a ceiling the pack promises: `check` refuses a node of
the pack that asks for the network with `network: true`, and
`pack audit` prints the value.

PackName.description: A pack name: one path segment: printable ASCII without whitespace, `/` or `\`, and not `.` or `..`

PackRequires.description:
What the installer's own config must provide — never satisfied
by the pack itself. `yunta check` and `yunta run` refuse a workflow of
the pack while the project or the machine lacks any of it, and
`yunta doctor` reports the gap; `pack add` installs the pack regardless,
so it can be configured for later. This type only parses what is asked
for.

mcp_servers.description: Names the installer must define under its own `mcp_servers:`.

programs.description:
Programs the pack's `bash` nodes and hooks start themselves and
assume are on `PATH`. A capability the project provides — its
lint, its tests — is a command the workflow names instead, and
never listed here.

Publisher.description: A publisher: one path segment: printable ASCII without whitespace, `/` or `\`, and not `.` or `..`

RequiredRunner.description:
One entry in `requires.runners`: a runner name the installer's own
`runners:` must define with a candidate. A pack names the runners its
workflows ask for, never an adapter, a model or a secret: the word is
`runner` in a manifest as in a workflow and on the log.

RunnerName.description: A runner name: a letter followed by letters, digits, `_` or `-`

SchemaRange.description: a schema range: whitespace-separated comparators (`>=`, `<=`, `>`, `<`, `=`) over whole schema majors, e.g. `>=1 <2`
